UnitStatement: TYPES.md is the authoritative vocabulary reference for Chirality App, defining canonical entities, stable identifier formats, enumerated values, agent roles, runtime vocabulary, and type targets.
Where a term is used differently elsewhere, this document governs unless a higher-authority source has been explicitly amended.
The project hierarchy is flat: {EXECUTION_ROOT}/PKG-XX_{PkgLabel}/1_Working/DEL-XX-YY_{DelLabel}/.
A Package is a flat partition of project scope; packages do not nest.
Each package contains references, active working deliverables, checking staging, and issued artifacts.
A Deliverable is a unit of production within a package.
Each deliverable has a stable ID, lifecycle state, context file, dependency record, reference record, and optional document kit or specialized artifacts.
An Artifact is a tangible output such as a markdown document, CSV register, tool-root snapshot, domain proposal, runtime event file, or validation summary.
Artifacts are authoritative only when placed in the proper project location and accepted by the relevant process.
A Tool Root is a project-level directory for derived outputs such as _Aggregation/, _Change/, _Coordination/, _Decomposition/, _Estimates/, _Reconciliation/, _Archive/, _Scripts/, and _Sources/.
The Instruction Root is the release-managed app resource tree containing governance documents, agent instructions, and framework materials; ordinary project execution must not mutate it.
The Working Root (projectRoot) is the user-selected local filesystem location where project execution state, sessions, artifacts, and git history live.
Project Truth is gate-relevant project state represented in versioned project files.
Runtime transcripts, chat drafts, UI state, API keys, SDK transcripts, and caches are not project truth unless a governed process imports relevant content into project files.

The Runtime Audit Mirror is the product-owned runtime event log, normally .chirality/sessions/<sessionId>/events.jsonl, used to reconstruct and review accepted turns, model output, permissions, tool activity, hooks, compaction boundaries, and subagent lifecycle.
Identifiers are assigned once and persist across renames and path changes.
Package ID format is PKG-XX or PKG-XXX (e.g., PKG-01), assigned by Decomposition / human approval.
Deliverable ID format is DEL-XX-YY or DEL-XXX-YY (e.g., DEL-01-01), assigned by Decomposition / human approval.
Dependency ID format is DEP-XX-YY-NNN (e.g., DEP-01-01-001), assigned by the DEPENDENCIES workflow/tool.
Scope Item ID format is SOW-NNN (e.g., SOW-003), assigned by Decomposition.
Objective ID format is OBJ-NNN (e.g., OBJ-001), assigned by Decomposition.
Session ID is an implementation-generated stable ID (e.g., sess_...), assigned by the Harness session manager.
Turn ID is an implementation-generated stable ID (e.g., turn_...), assigned by TurnEngine.
Runtime Event ID is an implementation-generated stable ID (e.g., evt_...), assigned by SessionEvents.
Subagent Run ID is an implementation-generated stable ID (e.g., subrun_...), assigned by SubagentGovernanceBridge.
Domain Profile ID is a domain-profile-id string (e.g., openpipestress), assigned by a future domain profile author.
Operation Proposal ID is an implementation-generated stable ID (e.g., op_...), assigned by a future domain operation workflow.
Folder names combine stable ID and sanitized label: Package as {PKG-ID}_{Sanitize(PackageName)}; Deliverable as {DEL-ID}_{Sanitize(DeliverableName)}.
The unsanitized canonical name belongs in _CONTEXT.md or the governing decomposition document.
XX, YY, and NNN are zero-padded numeric sequences.
Deliverable IDs use hyphen separators, not dots.
Stable IDs must not change unless a human explicitly approves renumbering.
Runtime event IDs are unique per event and never reused.
Type 0 (Architect) defines and maintains rules, standards, contracts, and role boundaries; scope is project-wide or system-wide.
Type 1 (Manager) interprets intent, decomposes work, routes specialists, and reconciles outputs; scope is project, package, or workflow.
Type 2 (Specialist) executes bounded briefs with minimal context and returns outputs plus evidence; scope is deliverable-local or narrow task.
AGENT_CLASS has values PERSONA and TASK: persona agents run interactive sessions; task agents run straight-through or delegated work.
INTERACTION_SURFACE has values chat, INIT-TASK, spawned, both, indicating how the agent is invoked.
WRITE_SCOPE has values repo-wide, project-level, deliverable-local, tool-root-only, workspace-scaffold-only, repo-metadata-only, none, indicating permitted write area.
BLOCKING has values never and allowed, indicating whether the agent may pause for human input.
Authority flows downward; escalation flows upward.
Type 0 defines what correct means; Type 1 prepares, routes, and reconciles work; Type 2 executes bounded work.
Humans approve, issue, sign, seal, and accept reliance.
A Type 2 agent cannot modify Type 0 rules; a Type 1 agent cannot issue work for reliance; no agent can approve professional work.
Persona alias HELP maps to canonical agent HELP_HUMAN.
Persona alias ORCHESTRATE maps to canonical agent ORCHESTRATOR.
Persona alias AGGREGATE maps to canonical agent AGGREGATION.
Persona alias RECONCILING maps to canonical agent RECONCILIATION.
Persona alias AGENTS maps to canonical agent HELPS_HUMANS.
Matrix row NORMATIVE covers guidance, orchestration, standards, and aggregation support; destination WORKBENCH.
Matrix row OPERATIVE covers pipeline execution categories; destination PIPELINE.
Matrix row EVALUATIVE covers review, dependencies, change, and reconciliation support; destination WORKBENCH.
Matrix column GUIDING helps orient or define the work.
Matrix column APPLYING helps execute or apply the work.
Matrix column JUDGING helps inspect, assess, or manage work items.
Matrix column REVIEWING helps aggregate, reconcile, or review work.
NORMATIVE row cells: Guiding=HELP, Applying=ORCHESTRATE, Judging=WORKING_ITEMS, Reviewing=AGGREGATE.
OPERATIVE row cells: Guiding=DECOMP*, Applying=PREP*, Judging=TASK*, Reviewing=AUDIT*.
EVALUATIVE row cells: Guiding=AGENTS, Applying=DEPENDENCIES, Judging=CHANGE, Reviewing=RECONCILING.
PipelineCategory has values DECOMP*, PREP*, TASK*, AUDIT*, the top-level operative category.
TaskScopeMode has values DELIVERABLES and KNOWLEDGE_TYPES, the dynamic scope mode for TASK*.
KnowledgeTypeOption values are Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, Procedure, Dependencies, References, Context, Status, Semantic, Memory; file-type buckets discovered from deliverable content.
DisabledOption is any visible but non-selectable option, a coming-soon or unsupported variant intentionally shown without enabling runtime selection.
Deliverable lifecycle states are tracked in _STATUS.md.
The deliverable lifecycle sequence is OPEN -> INITIALIZED -> SEMANTIC_READY -> IN_PROGRESS -> CHECKING -> ISSUED.
OPEN means the folder exists with minimum viable fileset; content is not yet initialized.
INITIALIZED means the document kit has been drafted or initialized.
SEMANTIC_READY means a semantic lens or semantic placeholder has been generated.
IN_PROGRESS means active human and/or agent work is underway.
CHECKING means work is under human review.
ISSUED means work has been released/issued by a human.
Stage gates such as 30%, 60%, 90%, or IFC are project milestones, not lifecycle states.

The INITIALIZED -> SEMANTIC_READY transition is optional; if semantic lensing is skipped, deliverables may transition directly from INITIALIZED -> IN_PROGRESS under the authorized actor rules in SPEC.md.
Dependency class ANCHOR connects a deliverable to a definition or traceability node; graph role is tree edge.
Dependency class EXECUTION captures information flow, prerequisite, handoff, interface, or constraint; graph role is DAG edge.
Anchor type IMPLEMENTS_NODE is the parent definition node, normally one per deliverable.
Anchor type TRACES_TO_REQUIREMENT is a requirement trace link, zero or more per deliverable.
Anchor type NOT_APPLICABLE is used for execution rows.
Direction UPSTREAM means the host deliverable requires information from the target.
Direction DOWNSTREAM means the host deliverable produces information for the target.
Legacy INBOUND normalizes to UPSTREAM; legacy OUTBOUND normalizes to DOWNSTREAM.
Dependency type PREREQUISITE is a required input or approval before work can proceed.
Dependency type INTERFACE is an explicit data or artifact exchange.
Dependency type HANDOVER is output consumed as input by another work item.
Dependency type CONSTRAINT is an explicit constraint or condition.
Dependency type ENABLES means the host deliverable enables downstream work.
Dependency type OTHER is a catch-all and is required for anchor rows.
Legacy COORDINATION and INFORMATION dependency types are not emitted in new extractions.
Target type DELIVERABLE is another deliverable in the project.
Target type PACKAGE is a package.
Target type WBS_NODE is a work breakdown or scope node.
Target type REQUIREMENT is a requirement, SOW item, objective, or acceptance item.
Target type DOCUMENT is an external or reference document.
Target type EQUIPMENT is physical equipment or asset.
Target type EXTERNAL is an external entity, organization, code, standard, or interface.
Target type UNKNOWN means the target cannot be confidently resolved.
Explicitness has values EXPLICIT and IMPLICIT, indicating whether the dependency is directly stated.
Confidence has values HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, indicating strength of evidence.
Origin has values DECLARED and EXTRACTED, distinguishing human-declared versus agent/tool-extracted dependencies.
SatisfactionStatus has values TBD, PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SATISFIED, WAIVED, NOT_APPLICABLE, the closure lifecycle.
Status has values ACTIVE and RETIRED, the extraction lifecycle.
AgentEnginePort is the product-owned boundary for running a turn, yielding UI events, recording canonical events, enforcing permissions, managing session linkage, and terminal outcomes.
RuntimeEngineContract is the formal expectations an engine adapter must satisfy before use.
EngineAdapter is a provider/SDK-specific implementation behind AgentEnginePort that translates provider-specific events, sessions, permissions, and tool names into Chirality-owned contracts.
ProviderAdapter is the concrete integration layer for an external agent provider or provider SDK.
FirstAdapter is the current concrete Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic adapter path; it is the first shipped path, not the strategic ceiling.
EngineConformanceSuite is the tests proving an adapter satisfies Chirality contracts.
TurnEngine is the runtime service that owns a single turn lifecycle and invokes the engine through the product-owned boundary.
SdkOptionsBuilder is the deterministic constructor for first-adapter SDK options from Chirality state and policy.
SdkMessageMapper is the first-adapter mapper from SDK stream messages into browser UIEvents and persisted HarnessEvents.
PersonaComposer is the builder for system prompt / appended prompt from instruction root, active persona, mode, and working-root policy.
RelianceBoundaryRegister is the record of product-critical semantics and their enforcement surfaces.

PiPatternCorpus is a reference corpus for stable agentic patterns observed in Pi packages and behavior; it is not a runtime dependency, adapter target, fork target, package import path, or spike authorization.
SessionRecord is a metadata record for a harness session.
sessionId is the Chirality session identifier.
engineSessionId is the provider-neutral adapter session identifier exposed by the runtime boundary when available.
sdkSessionId is the SDK session identifier used for resume; it is adapter metadata, not Chirality identity.
sdkProjectKey is the SDK project key or encoded cwd, if exposed.
sdkTranscriptPath is the path to the SDK transcript when applicable; secondary to Chirality audit events.
sdkSessionStoreKey is the key used by a configured SDK session store or mirror.
sdkConfigDir is the explicit SDK config directory when redirected to project-controlled storage.
events.jsonl is the append-only Chirality runtime audit mirror.
session.json is the session metadata/index file.
artifacts/ is the session-local artifact folder for large tool outputs and child-run outputs.
The HarnessEvent type target has fields schemaVersion:1, eventId, sessionId, optional turnId, optional parentEventId, timestamp, type, and data (Record<string, unknown>).

Initial HarnessEvent categories are session.created, session.resumed, turn.accepted, turn.started, adapter.initialized, model.request.started, model.delta, model.completed, turn.completed, turn.failed, turn.cancelled.

Later HarnessEvent categories are tool.queued, tool.permission, tool.started, tool.progress, tool.completed, tool.failed, hook.started, hook.completed, context.compacted, subagent.started, subagent.completed, runtime.mirror.error.
Browser-facing turn streams use compact UI events; provider/SDK messages are not the UI contract.
Browser UIEvent SSE event names are session:init, chat:delta, chat:complete, tool:result, session:complete, turn:error, process:exit.
Permission mode readOnly allows read-only tools only; write/edit/bash/network-capable tools are denied.
Permission mode workspaceWrite allows governed writes inside project root after hooks and policy pass.
Permission mode dontAsk denies unapproved actions rather than prompting.
Permission mode ask means the application may request interactive approval for governed actions.
Permission mode bypass is a developer-local escape hatch only, never shipped as ordinary mode, and still subject to explicit Chirality hard denies.
Capability policy is the Chirality-owned policy that decides which tools and capabilities are exposed and executable for a session, persona, mode, provider adapter, and validation state.
Explicit hard-deny precedence overrides allows at reliance boundaries, secrets, protected paths, release/professional claims, destructive actions, and unvalidated provider/network expansion.
The HarnessPermissionDecision type target has fields decisionId, sessionId, optional turnId, toolName, decision (allow|deny|ask), reason, source, decidedAt, and optional safeMetadata.
HarnessPermissionDecision source values are sdk-option, sdk-callback, chirality-policy, hook, human, prompt-support.
ask is an application-level state; SDK callbacks ultimately return an allow or deny decision.
SDK built-in tool is a tool supplied by the current first-adapter SDK, such as Read, Glob, Grep, LS, Write, Edit, or Bash where available.
Chirality MCP tool is an in-process deterministic Chirality operation exposed through SDK MCP tooling with mcp__chirality__* naming.
allowedTools is an SDK option that may auto-approve tools; not by itself a restriction boundary.
disallowedTools is an SDK option or Chirality wrapper policy used to prevent tool use or remove tools from context; participates in explicit hard-deny precedence.
canUseTool is an SDK callback or equivalent hook path used by Chirality to mediate permission decisions.
ToolResultStore is the Chirality artifact and preview policy for tool outputs.

Initial in-process MCP tool names are mcp__chirality__status_read, mcp__chirality__status_transition, mcp__chirality__deps_read, mcp__chirality__deps_write, mcp__chirality__scope_scan, mcp__chirality__scaffold.
Future domain tools use mcp__chirality__domain_* only after a governed domain-profile amendment.
Hook PreToolUse runs before tool execution and can deny write/shell/domain/subagent actions.
Hook PostToolUse runs after successful tool execution and may record provenance, budgets, and summaries.
Hook PostToolUseFailure runs after tool failure and records triage and safe diagnostics.
Hook PreCompact records the compaction boundary before SDK/model context compaction where available.
Hook Stop finalizes the terminal turn event.
Hooks SubagentStart / SubagentStop record governed child-run lifecycle where supported.
Claude Agent SDK is the current first concrete hosted runtime substrate for generic agent-loop mechanics; an implementation substrate, not product identity or strategic ceiling.
SDK transcript is the SDK-managed session transcript, secondary to the Chirality audit mirror.
settingSources is an SDK option controlling filesystem settings load; shipped builds use [].
SessionStore is the SDK session mirror/storage mechanism when used; mirror reliability is not assumed to be canonical.
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is an environment mechanism that may redirect SDK local config/transcript behavior if empirically reliable.
permissionMode is an SDK permission posture translated from Chirality mode plus capability policy and explicit hard-deny precedence.
bypassPermissions is an SDK mode not permitted in shipped ordinary workflows.
Pi pattern corpus is a reference source for agentic patterns only; D-APP-01 and D-APP-02 rule out Pi adapter, fork, package import, Node 22 sidecar, runtime-floor migration, and immediate spike work.
SDK terms belong at the adapter boundary; public Chirality APIs and canonical events use Chirality terms.

The ChildRunRecord type target has fields contractVersion:1, childRunId, parentSessionId, optional parentTurnId, parentPersona, agentName, projectRoot, mode, status, capabilityPolicy, governance, optional outputArtifactPath, and optional adapter.
ChildRunRecord status values are queued, denied, running, completed, failed, cancelled.
ChildRunRecord capabilityPolicy has inheritParentCapabilities:false, requestedToolNames, allowedToolNames, and deniedCapabilities.
ChildRunRecord governance has state (allowed|denied|adapter-observed), optional gate, optional reason, optional approvalRef, optional approvedBy, allowlistedSubagents, and delegatedSubagents.
ChildRunRecord adapter has adapterName plus optional adapterSessionId, adapterAgentId, adapterTaskId, adapterToolUseId, and adapterTranscriptKey.
evaluateSubagentGovernance is the authoritative fail-closed gate for delegation.
A Type 2 candidate is an agent instruction with AGENT_TYPE: 2 and preferred AGENT_CLASS: TASK.
Parent session is the session requesting delegation.
Child run is the governed subagent execution record.
Context sealed is the required governance condition confirming bounded context.
Pipeline run approved is the required governance condition for Type 2 task invocation.
Approval reference is a non-empty human/gate evidence string required before delegation.

The DomainEngineProfile interface has fields profileId, engineName, optional engineVersion, protectedPaths, proposalPaths, artifactTypes, operations (DomainEngineOperationDescriptor[]), manifestRules, and boundaryNotice.

The OperationProposal interface has fields proposalId, profileId, operationName, createdAt, createdBy, inputRefs, intendedChanges, deterministicChecks, expectedOutputRefs, risks, requiredHumanGate, and status.
OperationProposal status values are draft, ready_for_review, accepted, rejected, applied.
Protected path is an authoritative domain-engine artifact path not directly writable by agents.
Proposal path is an agent-writable folder for proposed changes, summaries, or review aids.
Deterministic adapter is a tool/bridge that validates or applies domain operations under profile rules.
Boundary notice is required copy explaining that Chirality does not approve, validate, or own solver truth.
OpenPipeStress fixture is a potential first domain profile fixture, not Chirality core.
Section 8 validation is the existing harness validation surface for baseline behavior.
Section 9 validation is new runtime validation IDs added as vNext phases land.
instruction-root:integrity is a packaging check verifying required instruction-root resources.
desktop:dist is the desktop build target producing a macOS arm64 DMG.
harness:validate:premerge is the premerge harness validation script producing a stable summary artifact.
settingsources_isolation validates that shipped SDK options do not load ambient user/local settings.
runtime_engine_contract validates that the engine adapter satisfies the product-owned contract.
sdk_session_link_resume validates that SDK session ID/linkage persists and resumes through Chirality metadata.
Priority P0 is required for current release usefulness, safety, or runtime foundation.
Priority P1 is important for quality, governed operation, or runtime maturity.
Priority P2 is later hardening, future extension, or desirable capability.

The framework separates how teams coordinate from how the system tracks dependencies; deliverable-local registers remain the dependency tracking substrate while _COORDINATION.md records the project coordination representation.
Coordination representation SCHEDULE_FIRST means Gantt or schedule logic drives sequencing while dependency tracking remains active for blocker detection and audit.
Coordination representation DEPENDENCY_TRACKED means dependency graph logic drives sequencing and handoff analysis.
Coordination representation HYBRID means schedule-first and dependency-tracked representations are both used.
Epistemic label FACT means directly observed in source text or deterministic output.
Epistemic label ASSUMPTION means a reasonable inference that requires validation.
Epistemic label PROPOSAL means an agent or tool suggestion requiring human decision.
Epistemic label TBD means an unknown value requiring resolution.
Epistemic labels help separate evidence from inference and prevent plausible invention from becoming project truth.
